samples.question: The cream board carries seven square tiles that never touch each other, plus small pale decorative squares lying on the bare board that mean nothing. Every tile is a 5 by 5 grid of cells inside a thick coloured frame, and every cell is either FILLED, showing a small dark square, or EMPTY, showing plain white. Exactly one tile has a navy frame and exactly one tile has a brown frame: together they are the RULE PAIR and they sit at opposite corners of the board, far apart. The brown tile shows the very same pattern as the navy tile after one single hidden CHANGE has been applied to the whole 5 by 5 grid. The hidden change is one of exactly four possibilities: a quarter turn clockwise, a half turn, a mirror flip left for right, or a mirror flip top for bottom. Exactly one of those four changes turns the navy pattern into the brown pattern, so comparing the two distant tiles cell by cell tells you which change is in force. Exactly one tile has a dark graphite frame: it is the QUERY, it sits at a further corner, and its pattern is unrelated to the rule pair. The remaining four tiles are the CANDIDATES; each wears a frame in a different colour taken from red, orange, green, teal, blue and purple. The four candidates are exactly the four results of applying the four possible changes to the query pattern, one candidate per change, so exactly one candidate shows the query pattern after the change that the rule pair fixes. Because all four candidates are turns or flips of the same query pattern, every candidate has exactly the same number of filled cells and the same amount of dark ink, and the frame colour, the tile size and the tile position tell you nothing about which one is right. The rule pair on its own cannot pick a candidate and the query on its own cannot pick a candidate: you must read the change off the two distant rule-pair tiles and then apply that same change to the distant query pattern. Which candidate shows the query pattern after the same change the rule pair shows? Give the colour of that candidate's frame. Answer red, orange, green, teal, blue or purple.
